acceptance: Producer::new returns Error::protocol before any network I/O when cfg.acks is outside {0, 1, -1}.
The acks(..) builder, idempotent normalization (acks=-1), and struct-update construction are unchanged.
client_api gains a no-I/O test asserting the rejection and a positive test that -1/0/1 still construct against the mock.
proposed_cards.deliverable: Constructor rejection of invalid raw ProducerConfig.acks values.
proposed_cards.title: Reject invalid raw acks at Producer construction

acceptance: Error::Closed Display no longer names a specific client (e.g. 'client closed').
Closed is still returned on the same paths (send after close, dropped workers, BrokerConn shutdown).
client_api asserts the Display text and send-after-close behavior for producer and consumer paths.
proposed_cards.deliverable: A client-neutral Error::Closed display string with regression coverage.
proposed_cards.title: Disambiguate Error::Closed display text

acceptance: Transactional produce receiving PRODUCER_FENCED, TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE, INVALID_TXN_STATE, or CONCURRENT_TRANSACTIONS fails the send and latches the same epoch-bump-required state as UNKNOWN_PRODUCER_ID.
commit_transaction without a preceding abort_transaction stays invalid from the latched state.
Non-transactional and idempotent produce paths are unchanged; mock-backed client_api coverage for at least one fenced and one abortable code.
proposed_cards.deliverable: Abort-required latching for fenced/abortable transaction produce errors.
proposed_cards.title: Latch abort-required state on fenced transaction errors

acceptance: Consumer::new returns Error::protocol before any network I/O when max_wait_ms, min_bytes, max_bytes, or max_partition_fetch_bytes is negative.
Zero and positive values keep current behavior; fetch builders are unchanged.
client_api gains a no-I/O rejection test per field.
proposed_cards.deliverable: Constructor rejection of negative consumer fetch bounds.
proposed_cards.title: Validate consumer fetch bounds at construction

No test that negative consumer fetch bounds are rejected (proposed KL07-15).
